authoringNotes: Original role-training exercises; local support policies stated in scenarios are assumptions, not universal legal requirements.
Uses the existing canonical Help Desk career path; the bank focuses on Help Desk Technician responsibilities.
Three authored distractor concepts expand into additional questions.

questions.prompt: Which service resolves a host name to an IP address?
choices: DNS name resolution
DHCP address leasing
Default gateway
Local print spooler
questions.explanation: DNS supports name resolution. An address lease, routed traffic and a print queue are different functions.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

distractors: Resolution of host names to addresses
distractorKnowledge.explanation: DHCP supplies leased network settings. It does not replace DNS name resolution or routing to another subnet.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

distractorKnowledge.definition: A next hop for traffic outside the local network
distractors: A service that assigns printer job numbers
A cache of recently resolved host names
A process that grants user account roles
distractorKnowledge.explanation: The default gateway is a routing concept. It is separate from resolving names, managing print jobs and authorizing user actions.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

distractorKnowledge.definition: A service that manages queued print jobs
distractors: A server that leases network addresses
A tool that resolves external host names
A device that routes traffic between subnets
distractorKnowledge.explanation: The spooler handles queued print jobs. A queue problem requires different evidence from a name-resolution or routing problem.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

questions.prompt: Which ticket note provides the most useful reproducible evidence?
choices: The exact error, affected device and observed time
A guess about the cause with no observed symptoms
A copied password used by the affected person
A statement that computers are unreliable
questions.explanation: Reproducible observations support diagnosis and handoff. Guesses should be marked as hypotheses; passwords should not be collected in ticket notes.
hints: Choose information that enables a reproducible handoff without exposing secrets.

questions.prompt: Under a support policy requiring identity verification, what should happen before resetting a caller account?
choices: Complete the approved identity-verification procedure
Accept the caller name as sufficient identification
Request the password and record it in the ticket
Bypass verification when the caller sounds confident
questions.explanation: The stated policy requires verification before changing account access. Familiarity or confidence does not establish identity.
hints: Check whether verification and authorization match the specific target account.

questions.prompt: Which first step best preserves evidence in a troubleshooting session?
choices: Record symptoms and collect relevant read-only observations
Reinstall the system before asking about the symptom
Delete all event records to create a clean starting point
Change several unrelated settings without recording them
questions.explanation: Observations establish a baseline before intervention. Destructive or simultaneous changes can hide the original cause and complicate recovery.
hints: Start from observed symptoms; isolate one supported hypothesis at a time.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command displays detailed adapter IP configuration?
choices: ipconfig /all
ipconfig /flushdns
nslookup example.com
ipconfig /release
questions.explanation: The all switch displays adapter details, including configured network parameters. The other commands query names or change local network state.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command clears the local DNS resolver cache?
choices: ipconfig /flushdns
ipconfig /all
ipconfig /renew
nslookup example.com
questions.explanation: Flushdns clears the resolver cache; it does not renew a DHCP lease or merely display adapter settings. Use it when the diagnostic evidence supports a cache issue.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

questions.prompt: Under a ticket handoff procedure, what should accompany escalation?
choices: Symptoms, impact, evidence and actions already attempted
Only the user name and a request to start over
The caller password and unrelated account secrets
A guessed solution presented as a confirmed cause
questions.explanation: A focused handoff helps the next team continue the investigation without repeating work or exposing secrets. Label unconfirmed hypotheses clearly.
hints: Choose information that enables a reproducible handoff without exposing secrets.

questions.prompt: Why should a technician test after each approved troubleshooting change?
choices: To link the observed result to a specific intervention
To make several hidden changes before recording anything
To guarantee that every restart permanently fixes a problem
To avoid collecting any baseline evidence beforehand
questions.explanation: Testing after an individual change helps establish its effect and supports rollback. It does not prove unrelated problems are fixed.
hints: Start from observed symptoms; isolate one supported hypothesis at a time.

questions.prompt: A workstation reaches a service by IP address but cannot resolve its host name. Which read-only test best investigates the name-resolution path?
choices: Query the name with nslookup and review the response
Reimage the workstation before gathering more evidence
Replace the keyboard because the address entry worked
Delete every account cached on the workstation
questions.explanation: The contrasting results point toward the name-resolution path. A DNS query gathers relevant evidence without erasing the workstation or changing unrelated hardware.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

questions.prompt: Ten users report the same application error at the same time. Which question most usefully narrows the incident scope?
choices: Which locations, devices and functions are affected?
Which desktop wallpaper does each user prefer?
Which unrelated password should every user disclose?
Which printer model should be replaced immediately?
questions.explanation: Scope and common timing help distinguish a shared incident from isolated device issues. Collect relevant evidence before selecting a remediation.
hints: Compare service impact and affected scope with the stated priority rules.

questions.prompt: A caller refuses the required identity checks but requests an urgent password reset. Which response fits the supplied procedure?
choices: Use the approved verification or escalation route
Reset the account because the caller expresses urgency
Ask a nearby stranger to approve the account change
Email the caller a copy of the previous password
questions.explanation: The procedure still applies under urgency. An authorized escalation can resolve a verification problem without granting access to an unverified caller.
hints: Check whether verification and authorization match the specific target account.

questions.prompt: Only one workstation fails to resolve an internal name; peers using the same DNS service succeed. What is the best next diagnostic step?
choices: Compare its DNS settings and query results with a working peer
Replace the shared DNS service without inspecting the device
Delete all application files on every working peer device
Disable the entire network security boundary immediately
questions.explanation: The affected scope favors comparing client configuration first. A working peer provides useful evidence while preserving the service used by other people.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.
questions.evidence: Failures are limited to one workstation; peers resolve the same name.

questions.prompt: Two approved changes were applied together and a fault began. The rollback procedure permits reverting one change at a time. What is the best diagnostic approach?
choices: Document the baseline and revert one change with verification
Revert random settings until the symptom disappears
Erase the change record to avoid confusing the next team
Apply both changes again repeatedly without observing results
questions.explanation: A controlled rollback isolates which intervention changes the result. Preserving the record supports subsequent investigation and recovery.
hints: Preserve the change record and test which single intervention changes the result.
questions.evidence: The fault followed two changes; neither was tested separately.

questions.prompt: A reset request names one account, but the verified caller owns another. What should support do under the account-access procedure?
choices: Pause the reset and resolve ownership through authorized verification
Reset both accounts because one identity was verified
Copy the account secrets into the ticket for comparison
Allow the caller to choose an account without further checks
questions.explanation: Verification must match the account whose access will change. Evidence for one identity does not authorize modifying another identity.
hints: Check whether verification and authorization match the specific target account.
questions.evidence: Verified caller identity does not match the target account owner.
constraints: Use the approved ownership escalation route

questions.prompt: A shared service fails while an executive requests a cosmetic desktop change. How should support prioritize under the supplied incident matrix?
choices: Escalate the shared outage and communicate its impact and status
Complete the cosmetic request first because of the caller title
Close the outage tickets because multiple reports are duplicates
Reinstall every affected computer before checking shared services
questions.explanation: The exercise matrix ranks service impact over caller seniority. Grouping reports can support incident handling, but it should not hide the unresolved outage.
hints: Compare service impact and affected scope with the stated priority rules.
questions.evidence: The matrix ranks a many-user service outage above a cosmetic single-user request.
constraints: Assign an owner and communicate progress

questions.prompt: A suspicious message requests a support password and contains an unexpected attachment. An unrelated outage is also active. Which plan best protects evidence and continuity under the supplied procedure?
choices: Report the message through security channels; continue outage triage safely
Open the attachment to learn whether it contains outage instructions
Forward the message and password to every member of the team
Delete all records of the message and postpone the shared outage
questions.explanation: The procedure separates security reporting from operational triage. Avoid interacting with the suspicious payload and preserve the information required by the security team.
hints: Protect credentials and evidence while following the stated reporting route.
questions.evidence: The local procedure forbids opening untrusted attachments and requires security reporting.
constraints: Preserve the suspicious message as directed
Keep an owner on the ongoing outage

questions.prompt: True or false: ipconfig /flushdns renews the workstation DHCP lease.
questions.explanation: Flushdns clears cached DNS information. Renew is a separate operation for refreshing DHCP configuration; the commands should not be treated as interchangeable.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

questions.prompt: True or false: under a procedure prohibiting secret collection, a support ticket should include the caller password for easier handoff.
questions.explanation: That procedure forbids collecting the password. Handoff should include symptoms, evidence and prior actions without exposing account secrets.
hints: Choose information that enables a reproducible handoff without exposing secrets.

questions.prompt: In Windows Command Prompt, enter the command to display detailed IP configuration for all adapters.
questions.explanation: The all parameter displays detailed adapter configuration for read-only investigation.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

questions.prompt: In Windows Command Prompt, enter the command to query DNS for example.com using the default DNS server. Do not add other arguments.
questions.explanation: Nslookup queries DNS. Comparing its response with the reported symptom helps investigate the resolution path.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.

questions.prompt: In Windows Command Prompt, enter the approved command to clear the local DNS resolver cache.
questions.explanation: Flushdns clears the local resolver cache. This focused action is different from releasing a lease or resetting unrelated configuration.
hints: Separate address configuration, name lookup, routing, and cached information.
